title: ff usage skill and a flow sized to the change
summary:
## Why

Nothing told agents when or how to use ff. One agent wrote its own 7-ticket plan in an over-budget session, published it through the library and approved it for the user: the grilling, the fresh planner session and the human approval gate were all skipped. And the full flow is overkill for one- or two-line fixes, so agents either over-process trivial changes or skip ff entirely.

## Agreed behaviour

**Three flow sizes.** The agent proposes one with reasons; the user confirms before work starts; when in doubt, the bigger size.
- **trivial**: about 10 changed lines or fewer, in 1-2 files; fixes or adjusts existing behaviour; no new API, CLI flag, config key or data shape; nothing left open. The agent edits directly, adds a regression test and uses the repo's normal commit/PR process. ff is not involved.
- **small**: one vertical slice one agent can finish in one sitting; the expected behaviour is clear; no design decisions left for the user; no migration. The agent writes one ticket JSON, then `ff ticket <file>` creates a standalone `ff:ticket` issue (no epic, no grilling). The user approves it and `ff run <ticket#>` runs the usual loop: red/green TDD, cross-model review, PR with QA steps, human QA and merge.
- **feature**: everything else (several slices, open decisions, new API/schema/config, changes across the codebase, vague requests). The full flow in a fresh `ff plan` session.

**Approval.** `ff approve <n>` approves a plan (epic) or a standalone ticket before implementation starts. It shows a Windows confirmation dialog listing what is approved and adds `plan-approved` only when the user clicks OK. Without a dialog it falls back to a `[y/N]` prompt in a real terminal, and otherwise refuses. The user can type `! ff approve <n>` in the session, or an agent can run it while the user clicks. Each approval made through `ff approve` is recorded as an `approved` event with how it was confirmed.

**Planner bypass.** `ff publish` refuses outside an `ff plan` session (`FF_PLAN_ID` unset) unless `--unplanned` is passed. An unplanned epic carries a visible note, and `plan_published` records `planned` and `size`.

**The skill.** `skills/feature-flow/SKILL.md` covers sizes, confirmation, commands per path and the non-negotiables: planning happens in a fresh `ff plan` session; agents never add `plan-approved` themselves (with `gh` or otherwise), merge, or edit or relabel ff issues; `ff approve` is run only so the user can confirm; `--unplanned` only when the user asks. Claude gets it through the plugin; for Codex, `ff doctor` prints the link command for `~/.agents/skills`. `ff init` adds a pointer section to each repo's AGENTS.md. The `plan-feature` skill starts a fresh `ff plan` session instead of planning in the current one.

## Out of scope

- Enforcing size limits in code; any ff tooling for the trivial path
- Turning an existing GitHub issue into a ticket; running one ticket of an epic
- An MCP approval tool; a separate bot GitHub identity for agents; blocking raw `gh issue edit --add-label plan-approved` (only the skill wording covers it)
- GUI dialogs on macOS/Linux (terminal fallback only)
- A by-size view in `ff stats`

## Notes for implementers

The robustness epic (#1) is still open and touches the same files: #5 (publish validation, injectable gh in `publishPlan`) and #8 (strict per-command CLI options). Build on current main. If #8 has merged, register new commands and flags in its allowlists instead of `BOOLEAN_FLAGS`.

tickets.title: Small path: ff ticket publishes a standalone ticket
tickets.goal: An agent can turn a small, well-understood change into one GitHub ticket with no epic: `ff ticket <ticket.json>` creates a standalone `ff:ticket` issue ready for approval.
inScope: New command `ff ticket <file.json>` in bin/ff.mjs, listed in USAGE. The file holds ONE ticket object with the plan ticket fields: title, goal, inScope, outOfScope, dod, tests, qaHints. `key` and `dependsOn` are optional and ignored. Read the file BOM-tolerantly (strip a leading U+FEFF) like other JSON reads
Validation before any GitHub call: title and goal are non-empty strings, and dod and tests are non-empty arrays. Otherwise exit 1 with an error naming the field

A publish function in lib/publish.mjs (e.g. `publishTicket(ticket, { cwd, approve, gh })`) with the GitHub module injectable so unit tests use a fake (follow the pattern ticket #5 added to publishPlan if merged; otherwise default to the real module)

The issue: label `ff:ticket` (plus `plan-approved` only when cfg.planApproval is false), no parent, body = `ticketBody` without the `Part of #<epic>.` line (make `ticketBody(t, epic)` omit that line when epic is absent)
Works without FF_PLAN_ID
Append a `plan_published` event: { planId: FF_PLAN_ID or null, epic: <new issue#>, size: 'small', planned: Boolean(FF_PLAN_ID), ...planShape({ tickets: [ticket] }) }
Output: JSON `{ "ticket": n }`, then `Ticket #n awaits approval: ff approve n` (planApproval true) or `Ticket #n is approved: ff run n`
outOfScope: Turning an existing GitHub issue into a ticket
A by-size view in ff stats; any size enforcement
dod: `ff ticket t.json` with a valid ticket creates exactly one issue labelled `ff:ticket` with no parent and prints its number
The issue body has the Goal, In scope, Out of scope, Definition of done, Tests to write first and QA hints sections and no `Part of #` line
A ticket with a missing title or goal, or an empty dod or tests array, exits 1 naming the field and creates no issue
With planApproval false the issue also has `plan-approved`; with planApproval true it does not
events.jsonl gets a `plan_published` event with `size: "small"` and the new issue number in `epic`
Running `ff` with no arguments lists `ff ticket <ticket.json>` in the usage text
`ticketBody(t, epic)` with an epic still renders `Part of #<epic>.` exactly as before
npm test passes and no test calls the real gh
tests: ticketBody(t) with no epic omits the `Part of #` line; ticketBody(t, 7) keeps `Part of #7.`
publishTicket rejects a missing title, a missing goal, an empty dod and an empty tests array, naming the field, and the fake gh records zero created issues
publishTicket with approve false creates one issue with labels ['ff:ticket'] and no parent; with approve true the labels are ['ff:ticket', 'plan-approved']
qaHints: In a sandbox repo, write a small ticket JSON and run `ff ticket` on it; open the issue: no parent epic, sections render, no `Part of` line
Try `"dod": []` and a ticket with no goal: clear error, nothing created on GitHub
Check `<git common dir>/feature-flow/events.jsonl` for the size "small" event

tickets.title: ff run runs a standalone ticket
tickets.goal: `ff run <n>` implements, reviews and hands off a standalone ticket exactly like a ticket in an epic, and refuses with a clear message any issue that isn't a feature-flow epic or standalone ticket.
inScope: lib/github.mjs viewIssue also requests the `parent` field (`gh issue view --json parent` is verified to work with gh 2.94)

A pure function in lib/run.mjs (e.g. `runTargets(issue)`) that decides what to run: `ff:epic` -> its sub-issues (today's behaviour); `ff:ticket` with no parent -> [the issue itself]; `ff:ticket` with a parent -> throws `#n is part of epic #E; run \`ff run E\``; anything else -> throws `#n is not a feature-flow epic or ticket`
runEpic uses it. For a standalone ticket the planApproval check reads the ticket's own labels and the log message says `ticket #n lacks the plan-approved label; nothing run`
Readiness and the skipped-ticket report reuse gh.isReady and the existing code paths (a standalone ticket already labelled ready-for-qa is reported, not run again)
Log file `<n>.log`, `<n>.usage.json` and events with `epic: n` stay as they are, so `ff stats <n>` works for a standalone ticket
bin/ff.mjs USAGE: `ff run <epic#|ticket#>`
outOfScope: Running a single ticket that belongs to an epic
Any change to the per-ticket loop (runTicket)
The exit code when nothing is approved or ready (robustness ticket #7)
dod: `ff run <n>` on an approved standalone `ff:ticket` runs that ticket through red, green and review and prints the results table with one row
`ff run <n>` on a standalone ticket without `plan-approved` (planApproval true) logs that the ticket lacks the label and runs nothing
`ff run <n>` on an `ff:ticket` with a parent epic exits non-zero with `part of epic #E; run \`ff run E\``
`ff run <n>` on an issue with neither label exits non-zero with `not a feature-flow epic or ticket`
`ff run <epic#>` behaves exactly as before
npm test passes and no test calls the real gh
tests: runTargets(epic issue with subIssues) returns the sub-issues
runTargets(ff:ticket issue with parent null) returns [that issue]
runTargets(ff:ticket issue with parent { number: 4 }) throws a message containing `ff run 4`
runTargets(issue with no ff label) throws `not a feature-flow epic or ticket`
qaHints: Create a standalone ticket (`ff ticket` once T1 is merged, or `gh issue create --label ff:ticket`), approve it, `ff run` it in a sandbox repo, check the PR and `ff stats <n>`
Run `ff run` on a child ticket of an epic and on an ordinary issue: clear refusals, nothing labelled in-progress
Run an existing epic to confirm nothing changed

tickets.title: ff approve needs a human click or terminal confirmation
tickets.goal: Only a person can approve a plan or ticket. `ff approve <n>` shows a Windows confirmation dialog listing what is being approved and adds `plan-approved` only when the user clicks OK. It works from `! ff approve` in a Claude or Codex session, or when an agent runs it, but the agent can't confirm.
inScope: bin/ff.mjs approve: view the issue. For an epic, the confirmation text has its title and each sub-issue's `#n title`; for a standalone ticket, its title and goal. Text built by a pure function (e.g. `approvalText(issue, subIssues)`)
If the issue already has `plan-approved`: print `#n is already approved`, exit 0, show no dialog

New lib/approve.mjs `confirmApproval({ text, title, platform, isTTY, showDialog, prompt })` with injectable dialog and prompt. Windows: a topmost Windows Forms MessageBox (OK/Cancel) via `powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive`. The dialog text and title travel in environment variables (e.g. FF_APPROVE_TEXT) and are read as `$env:` inside a FIXED script: issue titles are untrusted and must never be interpolated into the command

If the dialog can't be shown (not Windows, or powershell fails or is killed) and stdin is a TTY: prompt `Approve #n "<title>"? [y/N]`. Otherwise refuse with exit 1: `ff approve needs you to confirm: run it on a Windows desktop or in a terminal`
Add the label only on OK or `y`. Cancel or `N` prints `not approved` and exits 1 with no label
On success append an `approved` event { issue: n, via: 'dialog' | 'terminal' } to events.jsonl
personas/planner.md, publish step: when planApproval is true, run `ff approve <epic#>` yourself so the user can review and click OK or Cancel in the dialog; never add the label any other way
README: describe the confirmation and the `! ff approve <n>` option
outOfScope: An MCP approval tool; a separate GitHub identity for agents
GUI dialogs on macOS or Linux (terminal fallback only)
dod: On Windows, `ff approve <n>` shows a dialog in front of other windows that names the issue and lists its tickets; OK adds `plan-approved`, Cancel adds nothing and exits 1
`! ff approve <n>` typed in a Claude Code session shows the same dialog and works the same
With the dialog unavailable and stdin not a TTY, `ff approve` exits 1 and adds no label
With the dialog unavailable and a TTY, the y/N prompt decides whether the label is added
An issue title containing quotes, `$(...)`, backticks or `;` is shown literally in the dialog and runs nothing
An already-approved issue prints `already approved` and shows no dialog
events.jsonl gets an `approved` event recording how it was confirmed
npm test passes; tests never open a real dialog or call the real gh
tests: approvalText for an epic contains the epic title and `#n title` for every sub-issue; for a standalone ticket it contains its title and goal

confirmApproval: dialog returns OK -> approved via 'dialog'; dialog returns Cancel -> not approved and prompt is never called; dialog unavailable + isTTY + answer 'y' -> approved via 'terminal'; dialog unavailable + isTTY + answer '' -> not approved; dialog unavailable + no TTY -> refused
The PowerShell argument list built for the dialog contains no issue text (the text is only in the env passed to the process)
qaHints: Run `ff approve <n>` from Windows Terminal, then via `! ff approve <n>` in Claude Code, then ask the agent to run it and click Cancel: no label
Rename a sandbox issue to `a"; $(calc) ; 'b` and approve it: the title shows literally and nothing else starts
Check the dialog comes to the front even when the terminal isn't focused
In a Codex session the sandbox may block the dialog: it must refuse cleanly, never add the label

tickets.title: ff publish requires a planning session
tickets.goal: Epics can only be published from inside an `ff plan` session unless the user explicitly opts out with `--unplanned`, and unplanned epics are visibly marked.
inScope: bin/ff.mjs publish: when FF_PLAN_ID is unset and `--unplanned` was not passed, exit 1 before any GitHub call with: `ff publish runs inside an ff plan session (start one with \`ff plan\`). Pass --unplanned only if the user asked to skip planning.` Use a pure guard (e.g. `publishGuard(env, opts)`) so it is unit-testable

`--unplanned` is a boolean flag (add it to BOOLEAN_FLAGS in lib/opts.mjs, or to ticket #8's per-command allowlist if that has merged), so `ff publish --unplanned p.json` and `ff publish p.json --unplanned` both work; publish reads the plan file from the first positional
An unplanned epic's body starts with `> Published without an ff plan session (ff publish --unplanned).` followed by a blank line (epicBody / publishPlan option)
`plan_published` gains `planned: true|false` and `size: 'feature'`
USAGE lists `ff publish [--unplanned] <plan.json>`
outOfScope: Blocking direct library calls to publishPlan (ff eval uses it)
Detecting a planning session by anything other than FF_PLAN_ID
dod: `ff publish plan.json` with FF_PLAN_ID unset exits 1, prints the message and creates no issues
With FF_PLAN_ID set it publishes as before, and the event has `planned: true` and `size: "feature"`
With `--unplanned` in either position it publishes; the epic body's first line is the note and the event has `planned: false`
`ff eval` still publishes its plan through the library
npm test passes and no test calls the real gh
tests: publishGuard({}, {}) refuses; publishGuard({ FF_PLAN_ID: 'x' }, {}) allows; publishGuard({}, { unplanned: true }) allows
parseOpts(['--unplanned', 'p.json']) gives unplanned true and keeps 'p.json' positional
epicBody(plan, { unplanned: true }) starts with the note line; epicBody(plan) is unchanged
qaHints: From an ordinary terminal, `ff publish` a sandbox plan: refused, nothing on GitHub
`ff publish --unplanned` it: the note is visible at the top of the epic
Publish from inside an `ff plan` session: works with no note

tickets.title: One feature-flow skill tells agents which flow to use
tickets.goal: Any Claude or Codex agent working in a repo that uses ff loads the `feature-flow` skill, proposes a flow size with reasons, waits for the user to confirm it, and then follows the right commands and the non-negotiables.
inScope: Use the writing-for-agents skill when writing skill text

skills/feature-flow/SKILL.md, frontmatter `name: feature-flow`. The description triggers on code changes, bug fixes and features in a repo that has ff set up (AGENTS.md has a `## feature-flow` section or `.agents/feature-flow/` exists), and says it does NOT apply to agents started by ff to implement, review or escalate a ticket

Its body: (1) the three size criteria exactly as in the epic summary; (2) propose a size with reasons and wait for the user's confirmation, picking the bigger size when in doubt; (3) commands per path: trivial = edit, add a regression test, use the repo's normal commit/PR process; small = write the ticket JSON (fields and an example), `ff ticket <file>`, `ff approve <n>` for the user to confirm when planApproval is true, `ff run <n>`; feature = start a fresh planner as the plan-feature skill does; (4) what `ff run` results mean, pointing to the run skill; (5) non-negotiables: planning happens in a fresh `ff plan` session; never add `plan-approved` yourself (with gh or otherwise), merge, or edit or relabel ff issues; run `ff approve` only so the user can confirm; use `--unplanned` only when the user explicitly asks

skills/plan-feature/SKILL.md: stop telling the agent to follow the planner persona in the current session. If `ff config` shows plan.cli claude, run `ff plan --bg --name "<short name>" "<request>"` and tell the user to open it from Claude Code's agent view; otherwise ask the user to run `ff plan "<request>"`. Never plan in the current session
skills/run/SKILL.md: `ff run <epic# or ticket#>`, covering standalone tickets
README `Use` section: the three sizes, `ff ticket`, `ff approve`'s confirmation, and the skill
outOfScope: ff doctor and ff init changes (T6)
dod: skills/feature-flow/SKILL.md exists with frontmatter `name: feature-flow` and a description that excludes agents running as ff stages
It states the three size criteria, the propose-and-confirm rule, the commands for each path and the non-negotiables
skills/plan-feature/SKILL.md starts a fresh `ff plan` session and no longer tells the agent to follow the planner persona itself
skills/run/SKILL.md covers standalone tickets
The README Use section documents the three sizes and `ff ticket`

tickets.title: Codex and every ff repo can find the skill
tickets.goal: npm installs ship the skills, `ff doctor` tells the user exactly how to make the feature-flow skill visible to Codex, and `ff init` points each repo's AGENTS.md at the skill.
inScope: package.json `files` includes `skills`

ff doctor row `feature-flow skill`: ok when `~/.agents/skills/feature-flow` exists (link or directory); WARN otherwise (never FAIL) with the exact command from a pure function (e.g. `skillLinkHint(platform, pluginRoot, home)`): win32 `cmd /c mklink /J "<home>\.agents\skills\feature-flow" "<pluginRoot>\skills\feature-flow"`, else `ln -s "<pluginRoot>/skills/feature-flow" "<home>/.agents/skills/feature-flow"`. ff never creates the link and never links into ~/.claude/skills (Claude gets the skill from the plugin)

ff init appends a `## feature-flow` section to AGENTS.md if missing (pure function, e.g. `withFfSection(md)`): `When the user asks for a code change, use the feature-flow skill to pick a flow size (trivial / small / feature) and confirm it with the user before starting. Never approve plans, add the plan-approved label, or merge for the user. If ff started you to implement, review or escalate a ticket, ignore this section.`
This repo's AGENTS.md gets the same section
dod: `npm pack --dry-run` lists files under skills/
ff doctor shows ok when ~/.agents/skills/feature-flow exists and WARN with the platform's link command when it doesn't; this check never makes doctor exit 1
ff init adds the section once; running it again doesn't duplicate it
parseCommands still finds the `## Commands` entries after the section is added
This repo's AGENTS.md contains the section
npm test passes
tests: skillLinkHint('win32', 'C:\\pkg', 'C:\\Users\\u') returns the `mklink /J` command with both paths; skillLinkHint('linux', '/pkg', '/home/u') returns the `ln -s` command
withFfSection(md) appends the section; withFfSection(withFfSection(md)) equals withFfSection(md)
